title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks — Revised
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, artifact-anchored audit testing conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact match + fuzzy 5-gram + provenance heuristics) and a guarded exclusion policy on a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample. The preregistered primary estimand compared validator pass rates (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) using an exact McNemar two-sided test and paired bootstrap CIs. Execution produced no preregistered high-confidence contamination flags and identical validator pass rates for baseline and guarded episodes (150/150 each). Crucially, archived execution artifacts document two execution facts that render the prespecified paired confirmatory test uninformative for generation-level contamination: (1) the executed sample consisted of provenance-stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") rather than the public datasets listed in the preregistration, and (2) the pipeline ran with shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), causing a single model generation per item to be reused for both conditions. We (a) formally record this preregistration→execution deviation with artifact pointers, (b) reclassify the primary confirmatory test as degenerate under the executed semantics, (c) report exact, artifact-verified outcome counts and statistics, and (d) provide artifact-grounded recommendations (provenance-rich sampling, independent per-condition generation, per-item overlap persistence, and multi-model replication) to produce non-degenerate contamination audits for public benchmarks.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and framing. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for network operations (NetOps) tasks that translate high-level intent into device configurations or propose configuration repairs. Because operational decisions may follow from benchmark-reported performance, it is essential to determine whether measured success reflects genuine model capability or dataset contamination (items present in model pretraining data) and whether benchmark constructs match operational difficulty. Prior surveys and benchmarks recommend deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance tracing, and verifier-backed oracles, but systematic artifact-anchored audits remain scarce.

Research question and contributions. We preregistered a confirmatory audit asking whether conservative deterministic contamination detectors would (H1) flag items in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample and (H2) change validator-measured success when excluded and replaced according to a guarded policy. After execution we found zero high-confidence flags and identical validator pass rates for baseline and guarded episodes (150/150 each). The central contributions of this revision are: (1) a formal preregistration→execution deviation disclosure supported by archived artifacts; (2) reclassification of the prespecified primary confirmatory test as degenerate under executed semantics and explanation of the degeneracy mechanism with explicit artifact citations; (3) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory counts and test statistics; and (4) concrete, implementable audit design changes grounded in the archived execution artifacts to make future contamination audits sensitive to web-sourced benchmark leakage.

Scope and claim bounds. The executed evidence supports only narrow inferences about the synthetic, shared-generation regime used here. It does not imply absence of contamination in independent public, web-crawled benchmarks or across other model families. All core empirical numbers and procedural facts below are taken directly from archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the Disclosure Statement and the artifact pointers included in Methods and Results.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and validators. Recent system and benchmark work show that LLMs can produce configuration artifacts from intents and propose repairs; integrating formal verifiers or iterative generate–validate–repair loops typically improves average repair quality compared to naive generation. Formal network verification tools (e.g., header-space analysis and localized subspecification approaches) are practical oracles for reachability and policy correctness and are commonly used in generate–validate pipelines. Representative system and benchmark records are cited and verified in the archived bibliography.

Evaluation-validity and contamination critiques. Surveys and meta-analyses highlight two recurring evaluation risks: contamination (benchmark items leaked into model training) and construct invalidity (benchmarks dominated by templated or low-complexity items). Recommended defenses include deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap scoring, provenance timestamp checks, and transparent detector reporting. Our study implements a conservative subset of these defenses in a preregistered pipeline and focuses on documenting how execution semantics (sampling provenance and generation sharing) interact with detector persistence policies to influence audit sensitivity.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. We preregistered study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1 and froze: the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), detectors (exact normalized equality, fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds), guarded exclusion/replacement rules, sampling plan (task_count = 150), verifier and scoring rule (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, full_intent_constraint_validation), and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration targeted four public datasets (benchmark_scope: OpenAlex IDs https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W4404602270, https://openalex.org/W4404534210, https://openalex.org/W7166900660) but allowed deterministic synthetic generation for reproducibility. The preregistration and its hash are archived and pointed to in the execution bundle.

Sampling, generation semantics, and a required formal deviation entry. The preregistration permitted both independent_condition_generation (true) and shared_initial_candidate (false) semantics. The executed run used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce provenance-stable synthetic tasks (every manifest entry carries source_identifier beginning with "synthetic-netops:") and executed with independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics), as recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/model_configuration.json respectively. This constitutes a formal deviation from the preregistered benchmark_scope sampling plan (which targeted the four public OpenAlex datasets). We now explicitly record this preregistration→execution deviation and point to the archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/model_configuration.json) that document the executed choices; the full execution bundle contains provenance details and the execution manifest listing these files.

Detectors, thresholds, and persistence policy. The preregistered detector suite implemented:
1) exact normalized token equality (high-confidence flag on exact match);
2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence threshold ≥ 0.80 (medium bracket 0.50–0.80 for sensitivity analyses);
3) provenance timestamp heuristics comparing item timestamps to model-public-cutoff heuristics. The detector implementation persisted detailed per-item fuzzy-overlap outputs and full overlap tables only when a threshold crossing or replacement occurred (this detector persistence policy is recorded in the transformation_manifest). Consequently, when no items met high-confidence thresholds the archive contains an empty contamination_summary.csv and does not include a global per-item overlap table; we explicitly document this detector persistence behavior and its consequence for post-hoc overlap distribution reconstruction.

Guarded exclusion and replacement. The preregistered guarded policy deterministically excluded high-confidence flagged items and replaced them with deterministic retemplated items preserving intent similarity (embedding cosine ≥ 0.85) using fixed augmentation seeds. Replacement traces, embedding checks, and retemplating codepaths are implemented and archived; in this execution no high-confidence flags occurred and therefore no replacements were performed.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. Execution completed with planned_episode_count = 300 episodes (150 paired items × baseline+guarded) and completed_episode_count = 300 with zero failures. Because independent_condition_generation = false and no high-confidence exclusions occurred, provider call accounting shows model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item) rather than the preregistered maximum of 300. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm complete_pair_count = 150 and provider call accounting consistent with the shared-generation stage.

Contamination detector outcome and missing per-item overlap table. The detector workflow produced zero preregistered high-confidence contamination flags for the executed sample; analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged rows. As described above, the detector persisted detailed per-item overlap scores only when threshold crossings occurred; because there were no crossings, the archive lacks a global per-item overlap table and therefore we cannot report the distribution of per-item overlap distances to the 0.80 threshold for this run. The transformation_manifest records the persistence policy and is included in the execution bundle.

Validator outcomes and confirmatory statistics (artifact-verified). The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. All episode-level raw responses and validator traces are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json) and are the provenance for these numbers.

Representative diagnostic. A representative episode (pair-000001 / task-000001) shows identical normalized_reference_answer and normalized_response and validator_trace fields (parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, score = VALID_CONFIGURATION). Example episode files are included as representative artifacts in the execution bundle.

Reclassification of primary confirmatory test. Because baseline and guarded outputs were identical by construction absent flagged exclusions, the prespecified primary confirmatory test became uninformative (degenerate) under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics. We therefore treat the McNemar result as a diagnostic artifact of execution choices, not a substantive confirmatory finding about contamination prevalence in public benchmarks. The archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, deterministic_reconciliation.json) document this degeneracy mechanism.
sections.discussion:
Why the prespecified test was degenerate (artifact-grounded diagnosis). Two execution facts documented in the archive jointly produced the observed concordance: (1) synthetic provenance: the sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic tasks (source_identifier starting with "synthetic-netops:") generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 rather than the public OpenAlex datasets named in the preregistration; (2) shared generation semantics: independent_condition_generation was set to false so a single model generation per item was reused across baseline and guarded episodes. In combination, these facts mean that unless the detector produced a high-confidence exclusion and triggered a replacement, baseline and guarded episodes are identical and cannot produce discordant pairs (n10 or n01).

Detector persistence choice and interpretability tradeoff. The detector implementation persisted detailed overlap scores only on threshold crossings to reduce storage. This documented engineering choice (transformation_manifest) is legitimate for many runs but reduces post-hoc interpretability when no flags occur: archivists and auditors cannot reconstruct how close items were to the threshold without persistent per-item scores. For transparent future audits we therefore recommend always persisting per-item overlap scores (even when no threshold is crossed) so overlap distributions and sensitivity analyses can be reconstructed from the archive.

Power and design implications (artifact-backed). The preregistration's power guidance shows that independent generations per condition and multi-model replication materially increase the chance of observing discordant outcomes when contamination or paraphrased leakage exists. The executed single-generation-per-item regime reduces independent trials (model_calls_used = 150) and thus lowers expected discordance for the same underlying contamination prevalence. For contamination detection in web-sourced benchmarks we recommend: (a) sample provenance-rich public items, (b) set independent_condition_generation = true, (c) persist all per-item overlap scores, and (d) perform multi-model replication with multiple seeds; each recommendation follows directly from gaps visible in the archived artifacts (model_calls_used count, empty contamination_summary.csv, absence of per-item overlap table).

Operational takeaways. Deterministic validators remain valuable: the archived validator traces provide fine-grained evidence that each configuration satisfied the registered task constraints. However, auditors and practitioners must avoid extrapolating a synthetic/ shared-generation null to public benchmarks. The archive supports only the narrow artifact-grounded inference that, under deterministic synthetic sampling and shared-generation semantics, preregistered conservative detectors produced no high-confidence flags and the guarded policy made no changes.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors in an LLM-for-NetOps pipeline. The run produced zero high-confidence flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline and guarded). Artifact evidence shows this was driven by provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared_initial_candidate generation semantics; as a result, the preregistered primary confirmatory test was rendered uninformative for detecting generation-level contamination under these execution choices. We formally record the preregistration→execution deviation, reclassify the primary test as degenerate for this run, and provide artifact-grounded design changes (provenance-rich public sampling, independent per-condition generation, per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication, and paraphrase-sensitive detectors with human adjudication) to produce non-degenerate contamination audits of web-sourced benchmarks. All reported numbers, provider-call accounting, and validator traces are archived in the execution bundle and are the provenance for the claims above.

Representative executed artifact paths (archive) include: execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/contamination_summary.csv, and transformation_manifest (detector persistence policy). No manual human editing of technical content, analyses, references, figures, tables, captions, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

Executed sample provenance: items were provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") for this run; absence of high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require paraphrase-sensitive detectors plus human adjudication.

Passing the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
